text_blocks.answer: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and fine-tuning are distinct methods for customizing large language models: RAG supplies external live data at query time, while permanently trains model weights on specific domains or behaviors.
RAG Mechanism: Fetches external documents (like PDFs or databases) at runtime and attaches them to the prompt.
Fine-Tuning Mechanism: Adjusts internal network weights using a targeted dataset to internalize style, tone, or specific tasks.
Data Updates: RAG allows instant, dynamic updates without changing the model; fine-tuning requires retraining whenever knowledge changes.
Freshness: Essential for real-time data, live news, or constantly changing inventories.
Traceability: Provides source citations to reduce hallucinations and verify facts.
Setup: Lower initial training cost and easier implementation for general question-answering.
Style & Behavior: Best for teaching unique formatting, specific conversational tones, or rigid task outputs.
: Yields faster inference and lower runtime prompt overhead once deployed.
Domain Expertise: Excels when a smaller model needs deeply specialized reasoning on stable data.
If you want to explore further, tell me:I can recommend whether RAG, fine-tuning, or a hybrid approach fits best.

Fine-Tuning Mechanism: Adjusts internal network weights using a targeted dataset to internalize style, tone, or specific tasks.
